propositions: Four AST-based guards that scan single hardcoded source files produce zero matches because their policed constructs were relocated to sibling modules during refactoring, rendering the guards silently vacuous and unfallable

Guards F1-F4 lack anti-vacuity assertions and scan population derivation, allowing structural test brittleness to persist across module splits, whereas survivor guards (test_acli_graph_pagination_heldout.py:630) prove that explicit coverage assertions prevent silent disarming

Repair strategy requires (a) deriving scan population via transitive closure of package imports rather than pinning filenames, (b) adding landmark assertions verifying the population contains the policed construct, and (c) adding mutation tests that confirm the guard turns RED when the construct is planted at its real current home

Findings F5, F7, F8 are either low-risk vacuity without anti-vacuity assertions or false positives; F7 is architecturally correct (backend delegates are not transport policy) and F8 mismatches substring with roster construct
